title: Programmed movement & reveal
rule: Travel only the resolved path, ending at the authoritative tile and facing; reveal conveys the real register.

ideas.title: Floor receipt
ideas.action: Robot grips a receipt printed from its own chest and reels itself along it; the paper tears precisely at the destination tile.

ideas.title: Feet arrive first
ideas.action: Detachable feet scuttle to the next legal tile, stop expectantly, then the chassis concertinas forward to catch them.

ideas.title: Shelf-label flipbook
ideas.action: Each traversed tile flips like a shelf price label, carrying a successive pose of the robot until the real chassis steps out at the end.

ideas.title: Register jack-in-a-box
ideas.action: The revealed movement card opens as a tiny loading ramp; the robot rolls off it and follows only the programmed path.

ideas.title: Cart wheel conspiracy
ideas.action: Three wheels politely align while one stubborn caster points elsewhere; all snap straight together and deliver the exact commanded distance.

title: Programmed turning
rule: End at the same tile with exactly the commanded orientation.

ideas.title: Head files a request
ideas.action: Head rotates first, taps the unresponsive body, then the chassis reluctantly swivels to the same legal facing.

ideas.title: Price-gun pivot
ideas.action: A tiny price gun anchors to the floor and retracts its label tape, pulling the body around the tile center.

ideas.title: Unscrew and reseat
ideas.action: The robot lifts like a screw turning out of its base, rotates the commanded amount, and drops back into its threads.

ideas.title: Aisle sign betrayal
ideas.action: An overhead aisle arrow rotates the correct way; the robot stares, rotates to obey, and the sign folds into its head.

ideas.title: One-foot compass
ideas.action: One foot pins the tile center while the other draws a quarter-circle squeak; the torso overshoots cosmetically and settles to the exact facing.

title: Single robot push
rule: Both robots follow the resolved push path; no extra displacement, rotation, or damage.

ideas.title: Courtesy handle
ideas.action: The target involuntarily unfolds a shopping-cart handle; the pusher takes it, escorts it one legal tile, and the handle snaps shut.

ideas.title: Accordion apology
ideas.action: Contact compresses the target into an accordion; its front unfolds to the destination and its rear catches up with an apologetic bow.

ideas.title: Static-cling handoff
ideas.action: The robots stick cheek to cheek at contact, peel apart with a stretched static silhouette, and land on their resolved tiles.

ideas.title: Casual lean
ideas.action: The pusher leans like a shopper waiting in line; the target slowly realizes it is moving and frantically carries its own feet forward.

ideas.title: Receipt of displacement
ideas.action: At contact the target prints a tiny receipt, checks the one-tile charge, then glides to the legally assigned square in offended dignity.

title: Chain pushes
rule: The entire legal chain shifts together; a blocked chain stays in place.

ideas.title: Nested shopping carts
ideas.action: Robots telescope briefly into cart-like nested silhouettes; the compressed line extends one tile farther and each body reappears at its resolved position.

ideas.title: Complaint travels backward
ideas.action: Each robot taps the next shoulder as the chain moves; the last robot's offended look passes backward faster than the shove.

ideas.title: Borrowed legs
ideas.action: Each chassis stays upright while legs beneath the whole line run like one many-legged creature, delivering the chain's exact displacement.

ideas.title: Desk-toy compression
ideas.action: A squash pulse passes through the bodies like an executive desk toy; all bases move on the same rule clock despite the delayed wobble.

ideas.title: Queue tickets
ideas.action: Each robot suddenly holds the next queue number; a ticket strip pulls the whole line forward and tears between them at the final tiles.

title: Walls & blocked pushes
rule: The blocked robot or chain remains on its original legal tiles with unchanged facing.

ideas.title: Wall returns the receipt
ideas.action: A receipt slides from the robot into the wall; the wall spits it back stamped RETURN, and the robot folds it quietly.

ideas.title: Chassis overtakes feet
ideas.action: Feet halt at the obstacle while the soft chassis piles up over them; the robot peels itself back into its original silhouette.

ideas.title: Painted doorway
ideas.action: The robot hurriedly draws a doorway on the wall, tries the painted knob, and watches the chalk door fall off as a flat sheet.

ideas.title: Wall has manners
ideas.action: A tiny mechanical finger emerges from the wall and gently presses the robot's forehead back to its own tile.

ideas.title: Force goes upstairs
ideas.action: The blocked shove travels up the robot's body, telescoping its antenna skyward before it retracts with embarrassed precision.

title: Leaving the map
rule: Robot becomes off-board at the resolved edge crossing and cannot interact until its legal reboot.

ideas.title: Floor sample
ideas.action: Robot lifts the final tile corner as if inspecting flooring, discovers there is no more floor, and folds downward with the sample.

ideas.title: Barcode scan out
ideas.action: The edge scans the departing robot into horizontal barcode strips that descend one by one, leaving its ID briefly on a dangling label.

ideas.title: Last aisle curtain
ideas.action: Robot pushes through an invisible stockroom curtain; the curtain's bottom swings outward revealing the drop, and both vanish below the edge.

ideas.title: Gravity checks the clipboard
ideas.action: The robot hangs beyond the edge while a little clipboard arm ticks a box; the body drops instantly, followed by the late clipboard.

ideas.title: Caster keeps shopping
ideas.action: Chassis drops out of view while its loose caster makes one serene circle in the air, notices the missing body, and dives after it.

title: Falling into a pit
rule: Robot disappears through the pit and remains off-board until the legal reboot.

ideas.title: Self-checkout bagging
ideas.action: The pit unfolds paper-bag gussets around the robot; handles rise, the bag neatly closes, then the entire package drops through.

ideas.title: Drain with dignity
ideas.action: The robot circles the pit rim once as a flat spiral, keeps its eyes level until the last moment, then its antenna plugs the hole briefly.

ideas.title: Wrong elevator
ideas.action: Tiny elevator doors stand up around the robot; a down arrow lights, the roof sinks into the pit, and the doors fold flat again.

ideas.title: Measuring tape rescue
ideas.action: Robot fires a measuring tape toward the rim; it measures the gap, retracts with a useless satisfied click, and the robot falls.

ideas.title: Origami parcel
ideas.action: Robot folds itself into an impossibly neat flat parcel that fits the pit, drops through edge-first, and leaves one packing peanut hovering behind.

title: Reboot & return
rule: Reappear only at the resolved reboot space, with authoritative orientation, damage, and timing.

ideas.title: Flat-pack assembly
ideas.action: A flat carton lands on the reboot tile; legs unfold, body pops square, and the head is screwed on facing the chosen direction.

ideas.title: Returns conveyor
ideas.action: A tiny returns hatch spits out the robot backward; it catches itself, removes a RETURNED sticker, and settles to the legal facing.

ideas.title: Receipt reprint
ideas.action: A printer beneath the reboot tile prints a full robot silhouette upward; the paper gains thickness and steps free as the restored robot.

ideas.title: Mop wringer
ideas.action: A maintenance wringer squeezes a ribbon of robot into the tile; the ribbon inflates to its familiar shape and shakes one last drip.

ideas.title: Inventory found
ideas.action: An empty dashed inventory outline is scanned; mismatched parts hurry into it, swap to their proper places, and the eyes switch on.

title: Robot & board laser firing
rule: Beam follows the actual firing line and stops or pierces exactly as the rules dictate.

ideas.title: Price-check beam
ideas.action: The barrel unfolds a barcode scanner; a narrow scan line locks onto the real firing lane and snaps into the actual laser pulse.

ideas.title: Measuring-tape muzzle
ideas.action: A luminous tape shoots straight to the resolved endpoint, becomes the beam for one beat, then whips back into the muzzle.

ideas.title: Borrowed spotlight
ideas.action: The robot catches an overhead lamp's cone, squeezes it into its barrel, and fires the compressed light along the legal ray.

ideas.title: Laser on a roll
ideas.action: A tiny spool visibly unwinds a straight luminous thread down the firing lane; the thread flashes and is snipped clean at the resolved hit.

ideas.title: Muzzle sneezes politely
ideas.action: Barrel pinches shut, swells, then sneezes one precise beam; a tiny shutter dabs the muzzle afterward while the ray remains exact.

title: Getting shot
rule: Show the hit and actual damage without changing the victim's tile or orientation.

ideas.title: X-ray groceries
ideas.action: The hit briefly reveals absurd internal shelves of nuts and bolts; one item falls to a lower shelf and the opaque shell returns.

ideas.title: Dent takes a walk
ideas.action: A dent from the impact travels around the chassis like a trapped bubble, returns to the impact point, and pops into a small damage slip.

ideas.title: Delayed customer service
ideas.action: The chassis reacts immediately but its face keeps smiling; a little loading dial turns, then the face finally catches up with an outraged expression.

ideas.title: Thermal receipt
ideas.action: A precise beam scorch prints a short itemized damage receipt from the impact point; the robot reads it, folds it, and pockets it.

ideas.title: Loose panel applause
ideas.action: A side panel hinges open on impact, claps shut, springs open once more in disbelief, then latches while the robot remains rooted.

title: Conveyors & curves
rule: Carry robots exactly the resolved belt distance and curve rotation; blocked/conflicting movement remains blocked.

ideas.title: Treadmill denial
ideas.action: Robot runs hard against the conveyor while calmly drifting the legal distance; it checks its stationary destination marker in disbelief.

ideas.title: Luggage carousel
ideas.action: Robot folds into luggage, rides the belt with a tiny handle upright, then unfolds at its resolved tile with the correct curve facing.

ideas.title: Belt eats shoelace
ideas.action: A dangling cable gets gently caught; the belt reels the robot along the legal path, then releases the cable in a tidy bow.

ideas.title: Checkout divider
ideas.action: A checkout divider appears behind the robot and escorts it down the belt; on a curve it swings like a gate to communicate the actual turn.

ideas.title: Floor walking the robot
ideas.action: Conveyor slats lift like small feet underneath a rigidly dignified robot, carrying it exactly along the resolved belt path.

title: Push panels
rule: Panel fires only on active registers and applies the resolved push without extra movement.

ideas.title: Stockroom drawer
ideas.action: The panel opens as an overfull stockroom drawer, nudges the robot with soft parcels, then sucks every parcel back as it retracts.

ideas.title: Polite doorbell
ideas.action: Panel rings a tiny bell; when the robot glances over, a padded finger gives the exact legal shove and folds back into the wall.

ideas.title: Shelf restock slap
ideas.action: A shelf sweeper straightens an invisible row of products, catches the robot as the last item, and shelves it onto its resolved destination.

ideas.title: Accordion wall
ideas.action: The wall expands as a concertina, pushes with its final flat fold, and inhales back into an improbably thin panel.

ideas.title: Pillow inspection
ideas.action: A puffy test cushion inflates from the panel against the robot, deflates with perfect flatness, and leaves the robot at the legal pushed tile.

title: Floor gears
rule: Rotate the robot exactly the gear's quarter-turn at the same tile.

ideas.title: Jar-lid robot
ideas.action: Gear grips the robot like a stubborn jar lid; the body resists, releases with a tiny upward pop, and settles at the exact quarter-turn.

ideas.title: Lazy Susan dinner
ideas.action: A display platter rises under the robot and rotates; a tiny price placard trails behind before snapping to the new front.

ideas.title: Escalator comb
ideas.action: Gear teeth briefly comb the robot's dangling cables sideways; the cables pull the body through the legal turn and neatly fall back.

ideas.title: Wind-up key
ideas.action: A key emerges through the gear and winds the robot's base; the torso follows after a springy delay and locks at the right angle.

ideas.title: Record scratch
ideas.action: The tile becomes a record platter, drags the robot through one precise quarter-turn, and the antenna briefly acts as a stylus before retracting.

title: Energy collection
rule: Show only the actual energy gained, respecting the energy cap; no tile or facing change.

ideas.title: Battery vending tongue
ideas.action: Energy cube drops onto a tiny vending tongue from the robot's chest; the tongue retracts and the antenna straightens with satisfaction.

ideas.title: Cable spaghetti
ideas.action: Robot slurps a short glowing charging cable like spaghetti; the last plug taps its nose before a single counted energy pulse enters.

ideas.title: Price label recharge
ideas.action: A tired LOW POWER label peels off the robot; the energy pickup rolls underneath it like a fresh label and the eyes brighten.

ideas.title: Hand-crank helper
ideas.action: A miniature arm cranks the robot's own side handle once per actual energy unit, then folds away exhausted as the main robot perks up.

ideas.title: Battery nesting doll
ideas.action: Energy cube opens to reveal a smaller cell, then a smaller one; the final spark hops into the robot and all shells close into one counted pickup.

title: Checkpoints
rule: Credit only the next required checkpoint, showing the actual new checkpoint count.

ideas.title: Time-clock punch
ideas.action: Checkpoint punches a tiny timecard protruding from the robot; the new hole becomes the actual checkpoint numeral before the card retracts.

ideas.title: Velvet rope approval
ideas.action: A miniature velvet rope opens ceremoniously around the robot, gets tangled for one beat, and snaps into a clean ring with the earned number.

ideas.title: Shelf stamp
ideas.action: A giant stock stamp descends, stops just above the robot's head, and stamps only its shadow with the earned checkpoint number.

ideas.title: Receipt crown
ideas.action: A receipt prints from the checkpoint, folds itself into a small numbered crown on the robot, then packs into a badge.

ideas.title: Security gate courtesy
ideas.action: Two tiny security gates scan the robot, almost beep, then bow outward while the earned checkpoint number clicks into place.

title: SPAM, Haywire & card replacement
rule: Show the real damage cards or replacement; only the resolved card changes gameplay.

ideas.title: Junk-mail slot
ideas.action: SPAM envelopes force themselves into the robot's mail slot; it posts them back out, but a conveyor quietly returns the same counted envelopes to its deck.

ideas.title: Misfiled instruction
ideas.action: The real replacement card crawls from a filing drawer, kicks out the SPAM card, and squares itself inside the active register.

ideas.title: Haywire marionette
ideas.action: A visible Haywire card briefly tugs the robot's cosmetic limbs with tangled strings; the strings straighten into the actual resolved command arrow.

ideas.title: Coupon avalanche
ideas.action: A tiny coupon curls out, then unfolds into an absurd accordion; it refolds into precisely the damage cards actually awarded.

ideas.title: Printer chews the program
ideas.action: The active card enters a jammed printer; rollers argue in opposite directions, then eject exactly the legal replacement face-up.

title: Shield & damage prevention
rule: Communicate blocked damage only when a real shield prevents it; the beam and board state remain authoritative.

ideas.title: Warranty umbrella
ideas.action: A warranty booklet unfolds into a tiny umbrella at the impact side; the laser beads on it and drains harmlessly into its spine.

ideas.title: Return-to-sender stamp
ideas.action: A shield plate stamps the incoming light RETURN, folds it into an envelope, and shreds it locally without creating a reflected attack.

ideas.title: Bubble-wrap armor
ideas.action: One clear packing bubble swells at the impact point, absorbs the pulse with a satisfying inward pop, and smooths back into the chassis.

ideas.title: Sliding service shutter
ideas.action: A service shutter drops over the robot a split second before impact; a CLOSED sign flips once and the shutter lifts immediately.

ideas.title: Laser lint roller
ideas.action: A little roller sweeps over the impact side and collects the beam as a bright sticky stripe; the used sheet peels off and evaporates.

title: Upgrades & special effects
rule: Each study is cosmetic to its named legal upgrade: installation, EMP, swap, tractor, or displacement resolves exactly once.

ideas.title: Tool chooses the owner
ideas.action: An installed tool hops from its blister pack, tries several mounting points, then clicks onto the correct robot without altering its position.

ideas.title: EMP store-closing wave
ideas.action: For a legal EMP, a circular wave turns miniature OPEN signs to CLOSED in sequence and they reopen as the effect ends; affected robots match the real target set.

ideas.title: Swap changing rooms
ideas.action: For a legal swap, two fitting-room curtains spin around the affected robots and open with their positions exchanged, preserving their authoritative facings.

ideas.title: Tractor tape measure
ideas.action: For a legal tractor effect, a tape measure hooks the target's base and retracts only the resolved distance, then flicks its hook free.

ideas.title: Displacement drawer trick
ideas.action: For a legal displacement, the target folds into a shallow drawer that slides along the resolved path and opens at its exact new tile.

title: Shutdown & wake-up
rule: Robot stays on its tile; activity and damage cleanup follow the actual shutdown state and round timing.

ideas.title: Dust-cover bedtime
ideas.action: Robot pulls a fitted showroom dust cover over itself; its antenna pokes through, retracts, and a small breathing fold settles to stillness.

ideas.title: Closing the till
ideas.action: The robot's chest closes like a cash drawer, eyes flip to CLOSED, and its last little finger carefully pushes the drawer flush.

ideas.title: Self-folding chair
ideas.action: The robot folds into a compact chair-shaped rest pose on its tile; on legal wake-up, the chair unfolds and the head emerges last.

ideas.title: Maintenance sock
ideas.action: A knitted cable sleeve rolls up over the robot like a sock; a maintenance tag hangs from its antenna until the round allows wake-up.

ideas.title: Wind-down orchestra
ideas.action: Every cosmetic appendage stops on a different beat; the last tiny fan keeps spinning, notices the silence, and finally folds its blades.

title: Race victory
rule: Celebrate only the authoritative winner after the final required checkpoint; no apparent extra race movement.

ideas.title: Employee of the minute
ideas.action: A store portrait frame descends around the winner, struggles to fit its antenna, then expands as a tiny nameplate locks underneath.

ideas.title: Checkout total
ideas.action: A receipt taller than the robot unrolls, its long item list snaps shut into one enormous WINNER line, and the robot peeks around it.

ideas.title: Podium from stock
ideas.action: Three flat cartons fold beneath the stationary winner into a display plinth; the top carton opens into a crown-shaped backdrop.

ideas.title: Aisles take a bow
ideas.action: Nearby shelf labels and lamps hinge toward the winner in a synchronized bow; the robot awkwardly bows back a beat too late.

ideas.title: Tiny grand opening
ideas.action: A miniature ribbon stretches between the winner's hands; its scissors are absurdly small, but one snip unfurls a full-width victory banner behind it.
